prod_004:n1.prompt:
You are helping me set up error tracking for my application. The error-tracking vendor is {{vendor}}. If you don't already know, please ask me for: (1) which platform/language my application uses (so you pick the right SDK), (2) my {{vendor}} organization/account details or confirm I have configured credentials for it, and (3) the name I'd like to give the new project (e.g., my repo or service name).

Once you have that, please:
1. Using {{vendor}}'s documented public API or official CLI (with my configured credentials), create a new project scoped to the platform/language I specified.
2. Retrieve and note the project's DSN (or equivalent client key) and the project slug/ID, since these will be needed for SDK setup and later steps like alerting and release tracking.
3. Confirm the project appears correctly in {{vendor}}'s dashboard, with the right platform and settings.
4. Draft a short summary showing: project name, platform, DSN/client key (masked appropriately, do not print the full secret), and project slug/ID.
5. Do NOT apply any further configuration changes (alert rules, integrations, release tracking setup) beyond creating this project — this step is scoped only to project creation.

Because approval is required before changes are applied, prepare everything (the project creation request, the exact parameters you plan to use, and the draft summary above) and present it to me for review, but do not execute the creation until I explicitly approve it. After I approve, execute it, then report back with: the project name, platform, project slug/ID, and confirmation that the DSN/client key was successfully generated (masked). If anything fails (auth error, naming conflict, etc.), report the exact error and stop for human sign-off.

prod_004:n2.prompt:
You are helping me configure alert rules for error monitoring in {{vendor}} (our chosen observability platform). Before starting, ask me for: (1) my {{vendor}} organization/project details or dashboard URL, (2) the notification channels I want used (e.g., email, Slack, PagerDuty) and their target addresses/integrations, (3) the error/issue thresholds or conditions I care about (e.g., new issue types, spike in event frequency, regression of resolved issues, specific error levels), and (4) any grouping or silencing preferences to avoid alert fatigue.

Using your configured credentials, do the following:
1. Review our current project setup in {{vendor}} and identify existing alert rules, if any.
2. Draft a set of alert rules covering: new issue detection, error frequency spikes, regressions, and anomaly/outlier detection if the platform supports threshold-free detection.
3. Where possible, define these rules in a repeatable format (JSON, Terraform, or API payload) so they can be version-controlled, and prepare the actual rule configuration in the {{vendor}} UI or config file as a fallback.
4. Configure routing so alerts go to the correct notification channels, with sensible grouping and silencing rules to prevent duplicate or noisy alerts.
5. If {{vendor}} supports automated actions triggered by alert events (e.g., auto-creating tickets, triggering webhooks), draft those rule definitions as well, clearly marked as proposed.
6. Compile a summary document listing every proposed alert rule, its trigger condition, routing destination, and rationale.

Do not apply, save, or activate any alert rule changes in {{vendor}} — a human must explicitly approve before changes are applied. Prepare everything as drafts or pending configurations and then stop for human sign-off. Report back with the full list of proposed rules, the format they're in (UI draft vs. code), and any open questions needing my input before approval.

prod_004:n3.prompt:
You are helping me connect {{vendor}} error-tracking alerts to our team chat so error notifications reach the right channel with sensible routing, grouping, and silencing rules. Please do the following:

1. Ask me for: (a) the {{vendor}} project/organization details for our error tracking setup, (b) the team chat platform we use (e.g., Slack, Microsoft Teams, Discord) and the target channel name(s), and (c) any severity/routing preferences (e.g., critical errors to one channel, warnings to another, silencing rules for known noisy alerts).

2. Using your configured credentials, review our {{vendor}} project's alerting configuration and identify how to set up a webhook-based integration that subscribes to error/issue events and posts them to the specified team chat channel.

3. Draft the exact alert rule configuration: which events trigger notifications, how they should be grouped (e.g., by issue, by release, by severity), any silencing/muting conditions, and the webhook endpoint or integration target that {{vendor}} would need to point at our chat platform's incoming webhook.

4. Prepare a clear checklist summarizing: the webhook URL or integration target to be used, the routing/grouping/silencing rules, and which chat channel(s) will receive which alert types.

5. Do NOT apply, save, or activate any configuration changes in {{vendor}} or the chat platform. Present the full draft configuration and checklist to me for review.

When done, report back with: the proposed alert routing rules, the webhook/integration target, the grouping and silencing logic, and the checklist — then stop for human sign-off before any changes are applied.

prod_004:n4.prompt:
You are helping me set up release tracking in {{vendor}}, our error-monitoring tool, so we can correlate regressions with specific deploys and configuration changes. If you don't already know it, ask me for: (1) our {{vendor}} account/organization and project name(s), (2) how we identify a release (e.g., git commit SHA, version tag, or build number), and (3) our deployment or CI/CD process so releases can be created automatically going forward.

Using my configured credentials, please:
1. Confirm access to the {{vendor}} project(s) tied to our application.
2. Create a new release record in {{vendor}} using our chosen release identifier (commit SHA or version tag), associating it with the correct project(s) and environment (e.g., production, staging).
3. If our codebase or CI config is available, add or update the integration/config so future deploys automatically create a release in {{vendor}} (e.g., via a build script step, CI pipeline step, or SDK configuration that tags events with the release identifier).
4. Verify that new error events will be tagged with the release identifier so issues can be grouped and regressions traced back to specific deploys.
5. Confirm that {{vendor}}'s regression detection or deploy-correlation view is populated once the release exists (it may need a subsequent deploy or test event to show data).

Done looks like: a release is visible in {{vendor}} for our current version/commit, our error-tracking SDK or CI pipeline is configured to tag future events with release identifiers, and we can see (or will be able to see, once traffic occurs) which release introduced which errors.

Report back with: the release identifier scheme we used, what was configured automatically vs. what still needs manual CI/CD wiring, any config file or pipeline changes made, and next steps if further integration is needed.

prod_004:n5.prompt:
You are helping me install the Sentry SDK into my codebase to enable error tracking. Before starting, ask me for: (1) my project's programming language/framework (e.g., Node.js, Python/Django, React, etc.), (2) the repository path or location of the codebase you should work in, and (3) confirmation of whether I already have a Sentry account and project DSN, or whether I need to create one first (if so, ask me to sign up at sentry.io and retrieve the DSN using my configured credentials).

Once you have this information: identify the correct Sentry SDK package for my stack, add it as a dependency, and write the initialization code (using the DSN as an environment variable, not hardcoded) at the appropriate entry point of the application. Configure basic error capturing, release tracking (e.g., tagging with a release/version identifier), and any recommended default integrations for my framework. Include sensible defaults for sampling rate and environment tagging (e.g., production vs. staging).

Prepare all code changes as a draft — either a diff, patch, or a new branch/pull request — so I can review exactly what will be added or modified. Do not merge, deploy, or apply these changes directly to the main branch or production environment. Summarize the files changed, the SDK version installed, and any configuration values I need to confirm (like DSN placement or environment names).

When the draft is ready, stop for human sign-off. Report back with: the summary of changes, the location of the draft/branch/PR, and any open questions requiring my decision before the changes are applied.
